newsitem.title: INDIA: Prudential in India health insurance talks.
newsitem.headline: Prudential in India health insurance talks.

text.p: British insurance giant Prudential Corp is talking to Indian firms for a joint venture company in health insurance and expects to announce a decision by the middle of 1997, its officials said on Monday.

"We expect to announce a decision by the middle of the year," Joseph Ip, deputy managing director of Prudential Corporation Asia told a news conference to announce the launch of $1.0 billion Prudential InvestDirect Asia fund.
"We are talking to a number of people," he said without identifying the firms Prudential was talking to.
Ip said health insurance did not appear to be a viable investment in India because of the lack of a sophisticated health delivery system. But it could become viable in the next few years, he said.
Prudential officials welcomed the government's gradual liberalisation of the insurance sector.

"It's a step in the right direction," said Eric Sandlund, managing director of Prudential Portfolio mangers Asia. He said opening up of insurance was crucial to long-term growth of the Indian capital market.

The finance bill of 1997/98 (April-March) released last month, opened up the health insurance industry to private Indian firms. This is the first area in insurance, now a monopoly of state-run firms, that has been opened to private sector.
Foreign firms can now enter the industry as a minority shareholder in partnership with Indian firms.
Ip said the Indian operations were Prudential's largest overseas business until 1956, when India nationalised the insurance industry.
